g.text: RaftDB development and deploy loop on EFS
the durable WAL is what survives a task replacement | one writer, never two
1. Local development loop (docker compose)
Edit the C++23 source, then
docker compose up --build -d
The raftdb service mounts the named volume
raftdb_data:/data/raftdb
RAFTDB_PORT=9100, RAFTDB_DATA_DIR=/data/raftdb
The named volume
raftdb_data
outlives
docker compose down
, so the local WAL and
snapshot catalog are still there after a rebuild.
That is the same durability contract EFS provides
in production - the dev loop is not a different design.
Exercise the canvas locally over TCP 9100
2. Publish an immutable image
GitLab CI builds, contract-tests and scans the image,
then pushes the immutable tag raftdb-COMMIT_SHA to ECR
The verified digest is handed to
cdk deploy
so the RaftDb container is pinned by digest
Where does /data/raftdb live?
[DEPLOYED] EFS access point
/raftdb/production/member-1
[REJECTED] ephemeral task storage
3. Deploy loop that keeps the canvas
ecs update-service --force-new-deployment
A single RaftDB writer owns the EFS WAL.
Two overlapping tasks would open the same
durable files at once, so the deployment
window is deliberately a gap, not an overlap.
There is no task-count autoscaling.
minHealthyPercent: 0 / maxHealthyPercent: 100,
so ECS STOPS the running task BEFORE it starts
the replacement task
SIGTERM reaches the RaftDb container
stopTimeout: 120 s - graceful shutdown stops accepting
clients, publishes a final checkpoint and flushes the WAL
Old task exits; the EFS access point has no writer
Replacement task mounts the SAME access point
/raftdb/production/member-1 at /data/raftdb
(transit encryption + IAM authorization, uid/gid 10001)
Selected snapshot and WAL tail valid?
yes
no
Validate and restore the local snapshot from
/data/raftdb/snapshots, then replay the WAL tail
from /data/raftdb/wal - recovery, not reseeding
Publish /tmp/raftdb-ready, then bind client port 9100
App container waits for RaftDb HEALTHY, then talks to
127.0.0.1:9100 with DATA_MODE=raftdb-only
Canvas, config, bans, milestones and placement history
are exactly what they were before the deploy
Startup FAILS instead of seeding an empty database
(missing, corrupt, incompatible or mismatched data)
Health command keeps failing because
/tmp/raftdb-ready is absent; ECS circuit breaker
rolls the deployment back
3b. Contrast: what an ephemeral volume would do
Task replacement discards the container filesystem
Replacement task boots with an EMPTY /data/raftdb -
no WAL segments, no snapshot catalog
Nothing to replay and nothing to restore
This is why the WAL lives on EFS rather than
on the task's own storage. The choice is not
about capacity - it is the only reason a deploy
is a rolling replacement and not a data wipe.
The canvas is lost on EVERY deploy,
and every restart is a fresh empty board
Post-deploy: periodic checkpoints keep publishing to the
S3 snapshot bucket under prefix production/member-1
(RAFTDB_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300)
